finding_verdicts.reason: Line 12 uses Markdown inline-code backticks around SKILL.md. It does not contain Ruby command substitution or executable shell syntax.
Lines 16-21 are a fenced Bash example documenting lark-cli command forms. The fence is Markdown syntax, and no dynamic command construction is present.
Line 21 is only the closing delimiter of a Markdown code fence. It cannot execute a command.
Line 23 uses inline Markdown formatting for the api subcommand. There is no backtick-based command execution.
Lines 27-37 contain fenced lark-cli research examples with fixed sample paths and placeholders. They document intended CLI usage without Ruby backticks or an injection mechanism.
Line 37 is the closing delimiter for the preceding Markdown code block. It is not executable syntax.
Line 39 combines a Markdown link with inline formatting for lark-cli api. Neither construct performs shell command substitution.
Line 45 formats a destination path as inline Markdown code. It does not invoke an external command.
Line 47 opens a fenced Markdown template that users can place in a skill file. The delimiter is documentation, not command execution.
Line 60 is a quoted Markdown prerequisite containing a relative link. Its backticks format the link label and do not execute it.
Line 64 is an escaped code-fence opener inside a displayed template. The escape confirms that it is literal Markdown content.
Line 71 is an escaped code-fence closer inside the template. It has no execution behavior.
Line 77 formats a placeholder permission scope inside a Markdown table. It is plain documentation.
Line 78 closes the outer Markdown template fence. It does not run the fenced content.
Line 83 documents a fixed lark-cli authentication command with a domain placeholder. Inline backticks only format the example, and no shell interpolation is used.
Line 39 links to a fixed sibling skill document in the same repository. It neither accepts user-controlled paths nor accesses arbitrary filesystem locations.
Line 60 contains a fixed relative Markdown link to the repository's shared skill instructions. This is a documentation dependency, not arbitrary path traversal.
Line 70 is a generic workflow placeholder that passes an identifier from one API step to the next. It gathers no system information.
SKILL.md is readable Chinese Markdown with YAML metadata and examples. Its character diversity explains the entropy score, with no encoded, encrypted, or binary payload present.

content.value_statement: Building reusable Lark automation requires consistent API research, permissions, and workflow documentation. This skill guides Claude and Codex through focused lark-cli skills for single APIs or multi-step workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains registered APIs, shortcuts, raw OpenAPI calls, and schema lookup commands.
Guides API research through lark-cli help and schema information.
Provides a reusable SKILL.md structure with metadata and prerequisites.
Documents permission scopes and authentication requirements for generated skills.
Shows how to describe data transfer, rollback, and parallel steps in workflows.
Recommends user confirmation and dry-run previews before write operations.
limitations: Requires lark-cli, valid Lark credentials, and suitable permission scopes.
Does not supply complete parameters for every Lark OpenAPI endpoint.
Does not execute or validate the generated skill automatically.
Raw API calls still require careful review of methods, paths, and data.

use_cases.title: Wrap a Lark API
use_cases.description: Create a reusable skill for one documented Lark operation with its parameters, scope, and authentication requirements.

use_cases.title: Design an Admin Workflow
use_cases.description: Coordinate several Lark API calls while documenting identifiers, failure handling, confirmations, and possible parallel steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Skills
use_cases.description: Give internal AI tools a consistent SKILL.md structure for lark-cli commands, permissions, and trigger descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a lark-cli skill for [operation]. Include the trigger description, command, required parameters, authentication, and permission scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for one known Lark API operation.

prompt_templates.title: Research and Wrap an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Research lark-cli support for [Lark task]. Prefer a shortcut, then a registered API, and use raw OpenAPI only when necessary.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the best command is not yet known.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [workflow]. Document each API step, transferred identifiers, required scopes, failure rollback, user confirmations, and parallel opportunities.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for workflows that combine several Lark operations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Production Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my lark-cli skill for trigger clarity, command choice, schema accuracy, scope coverage, authentication, write confirmations, dry-run support, and recovery behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before publishing a complex or write-enabled skill.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that searches meeting rooms by floor.
output: A focused trigger description for room search requests.
A researched Lark API choice with parameters and permission scope.
Authentication guidance and a clear result-handling section.

output_examples.input: Create a workflow that finds a room and then books it.
output: A two-step workflow that passes the room identifier into booking.
Separate permission requirements for search and booking.
User confirmation, dry-run guidance, and failure recovery notes.

best_practices: Prefer shortcuts before registered APIs, and prefer registered APIs before raw OpenAPI calls.
Verify command parameters and permission scopes with lark-cli schema or official documentation.
Require explicit confirmation and offer a dry-run preview before write operations.
anti_patterns: Do not omit authentication or scope requirements from generated skills.
Do not use raw OpenAPI calls when a stable shortcut or registered API already exists.
Do not create multi-step workflows without documenting data transfer and failure recovery.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates guidance for reusable SKILL.md files that teach AI tools to perform Lark tasks through lark-cli.

faq.question: Which tools can use the generated skills?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require lark-cli?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata requires lark-cli, and API operations require valid authentication.

faq.question: How does it choose a command?
faq.answer: It prefers a shortcut, then a registered API, and finally a raw OpenAPI call.

faq.question: Can it build multi-step workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides identifier transfer, rollback behavior, confirmation points, and parallel execution opportunities.

faq.question: Does it protect write operations?
faq.answer: It recommends explicit user confirmation and dry-run previews, but generated skills still need human review.
